questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Interesting nature and culture. University with good courses.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was easy, most of the needed work was done before arriving. The University has a student desk, that is very helpful and they mostly answered quickly per email.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I needed to go to the student desk to complete my arrival at the university, which gave me and the university the information needed. After this I got access to my timetable for my courses and the university's website for students, where the relevant information is found.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: It would be nice if you could get access to the information before arriving physically at the university.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I signed up for the student housing waitlist in the beginning of May - so sign up early if you want to get student housing offered by August.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I lived on Eggertsgata close to the university, which was apartments with your own kitchen and bathroom, which was really nice but a bit expensive.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: My apartment was nice but very expensive considering it is student housing.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The university has a helpful guide on their website. I had to apply in May, which was fairly easy, except for the fact that I had to choose courses at that time and the university hadn't published their available courses for the semester yet and it could not match my pre approval of courses from my home university, since I had to choose from a list.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The university´s international division has an email that can write - but I had to remind them to answer a couple of times. Physically on campus they have a student desk.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the courses I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Get pre-approval for more courses than you need just in case, since it takes a couple of weeks to get the approval.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level was more or less the same as at my home university, considering the reading volume and level but the exams were a bit easier than at home.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I had to do research papers in all my courses, had group presentations and in-class-assignments which was different from at home.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Transnational climate law, Themes on International and European Environmental Law, International Human Rights, Basic Course in Public International Law, The United States Legal System and American Constitutional Law.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The Basic Course in Public International Law was very interesting.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: The student housing did not have any furniture or kitchen utensils, so I had to spend a lot of money on that.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Housing and food was very expensive

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A lot of activities were available.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The university gym was very cheap but also very small.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Rent a car and go see the nature.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy, it is pretty close to the danish culture.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: A lot of people speak danish.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The language was harder to learn than I expected.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: It was easy to adjust to since it is close to the danish. I really enjoyed seeing the nature.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Start planning early, sign up for student housing early, rent cars and go see the nature.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Participate in the orientation days.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting people from all parts of the world and experiencing the beautiful nature of Iceland.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The planning before I arrived.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: I totally recommend doing your exchange in Iceland!!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
